entities.name: Allergic rhinitis
observations: UAE prevalence estimates vary by population and questionnaire definition; reported estimates include 7%, 32–36%, and 46.5–51.3% in different studies.
UAE-reported environmental aggravators include dust, grass/pollen, and proximity to animals.

entities.name: UAE AR school prevalence
observations: In a 2019 Dubai/Northern Emirates ISAAC questionnaire survey, allergic-rhinitis prevalence was 46.5% among children aged 6–7 years and 51.3% among those aged 13–14 years; evidence was symptom/questionnaire-based rather than physician-confirmed.

entities.name: Al-Ain AR prevalence
observations: In an Al-Ain random-sample questionnaire study of 6,543 participants aged at least 13 years, crude self-reported allergic-rhinitis prevalence was 36% and age/sex-adjusted prevalence was 32%.

entities.name: UAE AR triggers
observations: In a seven-Emirate ECRHS-II screening study, 7% of 1,229 participants had allergic-rhinitis symptoms/diagnosis; reported aggravators were dust in 59%, grass/pollen in 44%, and proximity to animals in 21%; 71% reported environmental triggers.

entities.name: UAE AR familial risks
observations: Al-Ain questionnaire analysis found associations of allergic rhinitis with family history, Arab origin, younger age, female sex, and higher education.

entities.name: PMID:34703522
observations: 2019 multicenter UAE school survey using ISAAC questionnaires; reported allergic-rhinitis prevalence of 46.5% in 6–7-year-olds and 51.3% in 13–14-year-olds.

entities.name: PMID:19735489
observations: Al-Ain population study; self-reported allergic-rhinitis prevalence was 36% crude and 32% adjusted.

entities.name: PMID:25097721
observations: Seven-Emirate ECRHS-II study; 7% screened positive for allergic-rhinitis symptoms/diagnosis, with dust, grass/pollen, and animal proximity as leading reported aggravators.
